(1) the performance of an algorithm for adversarial imitation learning is highly dependent on the choice of the discriminator architecture and (2) the choice of the critic and reward function has a smaller impact on the performance of the algorithm.

(i) adversarial imitation learning is a promising approach to learn policies for continuous control tasks, (ii) the choice of the discriminator is crucial for the success of the algorithm and (iii) the choice of discriminator and the choice of the reward function are not independent.
